source_text: Si nulla lex dei prohibuisset idola fieri a nobis, nulla uox spiritus sancti fabricatoribus idolorum non minus quam cultoribus comminaretur, de ipso sacramento nostro interpretaremur nobis aduersas esse fidei eiusmodi artes. quomodo enim renuntiauimus diabolo et angelis eius, si eos facimus? quod repudium diximus iis, non dico cum quibus, sed de quibus uiuimus? quam discordiam suscepimus in eos, quibus exhibitionis nostrae gratia confiteris? uerbo destruere quod facto struis? unum deum praedicare qui tantos efficis? uerum deum praedicare qui falsos facis? facio, ait quidam, sed non colo: quasi ob aliquam causam colere non audeat, nisi ob quam et facere nonn debeat, scilicet ob, dei offensam utrubique. immo tu colis, qui facis, ut coli possint. colis autem non spiritu uilissimi nidoris alicuius, sed tuo proprio nec anima pecudis impensa, sed anima tua. illis ingenium tuum immolas, illis sudorem tuum libas, illis prudentiam tuam accendis. plus es illis quam sacerdos, cum per te habeant sacerdotem; diligentia tua numen illorum est. negas te quod facis colere? sed illi non negant, quibus hanc saginatiorem et auratiorem et maiorem hostiam caedis, salutem tuam tota die.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that even making idols is forbidden, because it serves the demons Christians renounced at baptism.
pass_a_gloss: If no law of God had forbidden idols to be made by us, no voice of the holy spirit would threaten the makers of idols not less than the worshippers, from our very sacred commitment we would interpret for ourselves that arts of this kind are opposed to his faith. For how have we renounced the devil and his angels, if we make them? What divorce have we declared from them, I do not say with whom, but from whom we live? What discord have we taken up against them, to whom for the sake of our display you confess? To destroy by word what you build by deed? To preach one God who makes so many? To preach the true God who makes false ones? I make, says someone, but I do not worship: as if for some reason he would not dare to worship, except for the reason for which he ought not even to make, namely because of the offense of God in both cases. No, you worship, who make, so that they can be worshipped. But you worship not with the spirit of some cheapest vapor, but with your own, nor with the soul of a beast spent, but with your soul. To them you sacrifice your talent, to them you pour out your sweat, to them you kindle your prudence. You are more to them than a priest, since through you they have a priest; your diligence is their divinity. Do you deny that you worship what you make? But they do not deny, for whom you slaughter this fatter and more gilded and greater victim, your salvation all day long.

lemmas.gloss: you pour out as a libation
you slaughter, you kill as a sacrifice

choices.english: from our very sacred commitment we would interpret
choices.why: sacramentum is the baptismal pledge, the fixed glossary term; the verb is a potential subjunctive in a past counterfactual condition
rejected: from our very oath we would conclude
we would interpret from our baptismal vow

choices.english: for the sake of our display
choices.why: exhibitio here means the means of making a living, the public display of one's craft; gratia with genitive means 'for the sake of'
rejected: for the sake of our livelihood

choices.english: to destroy by word what you build by deed
choices.why: the infinitive continues the indignant questions; struis is second person singular present, so the shift to 'you' is kept
rejected: to destroy with a word what you build with a deed
to tear down by word what you build up by deed

choices.term: colis autem non spiritu uilissimi nidoris alicuius
choices.english: but you worship not with the spirit of some cheapest vapor
choices.why: spiritu here is ablative of means; nidor is the smell of burning sacrifice, so 'vapor' keeps the sacrificial image
rejected: not with the breath of some cheap incense
not with the spirit of some worthless smoke

choices.english: to them you kindle your prudence
choices.why: accendis means to light or set fire to, continuing the sacrificial metaphor of burning offerings
rejected: you light up your skill for them
you burn your wisdom for them

choices.why: salus here means the man's whole well-being and eternal salvation, which he spends daily on idol-making; tota die is idiomatic for 'all day long'

pass_b_english: Suppose no law of God had forbidden us to make idols, and no voice of the Holy Spirit had threatened idol-makers no less than idol-worshippers. Even then, we could draw the conclusion from our very sacred commitment that arts of this kind are opposed to our faith. How have we renounced the devil and his angels if we make them? What divorce have we declared from them? I do not mean from those with whom we live, but from those by whom we live. What discord have we taken up against them, when for the sake of our display you acknowledge them? Do you destroy by word what you build by deed? Do you preach one God while you make so many? Do you preach the true God while you make false ones?

Someone says, "I make them, but I do not worship them." As if there were any reason he would not dare to worship them except the very reason he ought not to make them: the offense against God in both cases. No, you worship, because you make them so that they can be worshipped. And you worship not with the spirit of some cheapest vapor, but with your own spirit; not at the cost of an animal's life, but at the cost of your own soul. To them you sacrifice your talent; to them you pour out your sweat as a libation; to them you kindle your prudence. You are more to them than a priest, since through you they have a priest. Your diligence is their divinity. You deny that you worship what you make? But they do not deny it—the ones for whom you slaughter this fatter, more gilded, greater victim: your salvation all day long.

problems.quote: when you acknowledge them for the sake of our display?
problems.why: confiteris is 2nd sg.; 'our display' misreads exhibitionis nostrae. It means 'you confess/acknowledge them'—the objector's own admission.
problems.fix: which you confess for the sake of our display?
problems.ruling: Latin asks 'to whom you confess for the sake of our display?' not 'when you acknowledge them'; prepositional nuance lost.

edits.old: when you acknowledge them for the sake of our display?
edits.new: which you acknowledge for the sake of our display?

fixed: Changed 'when you acknowledge them' to 'which you acknowledge' to reflect the relative clause 'quibus ... confiteris' (2nd sg. 'you acknowledge'), keeping 'our display' as the rendering of 'exhibitionis nostrae'.

problems.quote: which you acknowledge for the sake of our display?
problems.why: confiteris is 2nd sg. 'you confess/acknowledge'; exhibitionis nostrae is 'our display' (pomp). Subject is 'you', not 'which'.
problems.fix: which you acknowledge exists for the sake of our display?
problems.ruling: Latin uses ablative 'quibus' (instrumental) – 'with which you confess', not direct object 'which you acknowledge'.

edits.old: which you acknowledge for the sake of our display?
edits.new: whom you acknowledge for the sake of our display?

fixed: Changed 'which' to 'whom' because the source 'quibus' refers to persons (the devil and his angels), not things; the relative pronoun should be personal in English.

last_rejected.why: Tantos means 'so great', not 'so many'; the contrast is greatness, not number.
last_rejected.fix: while you make such great ones
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'tantos' can mean 'so many' (implied idols); translation fits context, not a meaning change.

polish.changed: Clarified the objector's voice, made the pronouns and the baptismal vow reference consistent, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and quotation.

notes.why: Baptismal vow rendered three different ways; reader may miss they are the same vow.
notes.fix: Use 'sacred commitment' consistently; note it means the baptismal vow.
